description: Before WORK (a `git commit`, or a build/test command), checks that the mandatory skills were invoked this session — a fresh per-skill marker in ~/.cache/agent-tools/skills-invoked/<session-id>/ (session-scoped by CC's own session id, so one session can't satisfy another concurrent session's check), with a lower-precedence fallback to the pre-session-scoping global ~/.cache/agent-tools/skills-invoked/<skill> path for harnesses/manual use with no session-aware marker writer. MANDATORY_SKILLS (default delegate-work-to-subagents,visual-proof-cycle), freshness SKILLS_FRESH_WINDOW_S (7200s). WARN first, BLOCK on repeat (default WARN-first so it never wedges while the marker-writer is wired), tracked by a marker keyed by cwd and, when a valid session id is present, that session too. A dispatched subagent (agent_id present) is exempt from the two orchestration/visual defaults (it IS the delegate; non-UI work has no visual proof) but still gated on any project-specific MANDATORY_SKILLS entry. No self-service bypass: request a one-time Telegram approval via RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SKILLS_READ_GATE='<justification>' (deny-by-default; bare 1 rejected) — allows only on the human's tg-ctl approval, which is why timeout_ms is 960000 (tg-ctl's live-Telegram cap). on_error=open.
